questions.question: How many pairs of false ribs are located above the floating ribs that are connected to each other by costal cartilage?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**3 pairs of false ribs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Humans have a total of **12 pairs of ribs**, which are divided into three categories: **true ribs**, **false ribs**, and **floating ribs**.
 
• The **false ribs** are the **8th, 9th, and 10th pairs** of ribs, located above the floating ribs.
 
• These ribs are called "false ribs" because they are not directly attached to the sternum; instead, they are connected to each other by **costal cartilage**.
 
• The **floating ribs** (11th and 12th pairs) are not attached to the sternum or any other ribs and are located below the false ribs.
 
• This arrangement provides flexibility and protection to vital organs such as the **lungs** and **heart**.
 
• Thus, there are **3 pairs of false ribs** located above the floating ribs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **True Ribs**__

 __
 
• The first **seven pairs of ribs** are called **true ribs**.
 
• They are directly attached to the **sternum** via costal cartilage.
 
• True ribs provide the primary support to the thoracic cage.
 
 
 
• **Floating Ribs**__
 
 
• The **11th and 12th pairs** of ribs are called **floating ribs**.
 
• These ribs are not attached to the sternum or other ribs, which makes them "floating."
 
• Floating ribs serve to protect the **kidneys** and other posterior organs.

questions.question: Who was the first Portuguese explorer to reach India in 1498, arriving at Calicut on the Malabar Coast?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vasco da Gama** was the first Portuguese explorer to reach **India** in **1498**, landing at **Calicut on the Malabar Coast**.
 
• This expedition marked the beginning of the **European Age of Exploration** and established a direct sea route between Europe and India.
 
• His journey was a key event in the history of **global trade**, as it opened the way for the spice trade and other goods between Europe and Asia.
 
• The expedition of Vasco da Gama was sponsored by **King Manuel I of Portugal**.
 
• Vasco da Gama set sail from **Lisbon** in 1497, rounded the **Cape of Good Hope**, and reached the Indian Ocean.
 
• Upon his arrival in Calicut, he was welcomed by the ruler, the **Samudri Raja (Zamorin)**, which paved the way for future Portuguese dominance in Indian trade.
 
• This voyage is considered one of the most significant achievements in the history of navigation and trade expansion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• Columbus never reached India; his voyages led to the discovery of the New World.

• He is known for capturing **Goa** in 1510 and laying the foundations of Portuguese colonial rule in India.

questions.question: Why does the eastern coastal plain have fewer ports and harbours compared to the western coastal plain?

options.text: It is closer to the Equator

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is an emergent coast**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **eastern coastal plain** of India is an example of an **emergent coast**, meaning the land area has risen relative to the sea level over time.
 
• Due to this emergence, the coastline is relatively **straight**, with fewer natural inlets and bays compared to the **western coast**.
 
• The lack of natural indentations and inlets along the eastern coastal plain makes it **less suitable for the development of ports and harbours**.
 
• In contrast, the western coastal plain is a **submergent coast**, which means it has sunken relative to the sea level, leading to the formation of **deep natural harbours** such as those in Mumbai and Kochi.
 
• The eastern coastal plain is also characterized by the presence of **river deltas**, such as those formed by the **Ganga, Godavari, Krishna, and Mahanadi rivers**. These deltas make the coastline less stable and unsuitable for harbour construction.
 
• The sediment deposition along the eastern coast further adds to its **shallow and unstable nature**, making it less ideal for establishing ports and harbours.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **It is closer to the Equator**__

 __
 
• This factor does not directly impact the availability of ports and harbours. The proximity to the **equator** mainly influences the **climate and temperature** of a region, not its coastal features.
 
 
 
• **It has more tourist beaches**__
 __
 
• The presence of tourist beaches does not determine the availability of ports and harbours. Tourist beaches are developed based on **scenic beauty, accessibility, and amenities**, whereas harbours depend on **natural coastal features**.
 
 
 
• **It receives more rainfall**__
 
 
• While the eastern coastal plain does receive significant rainfall, especially during the **northeast monsoon**, rainfall does not directly impact the suitability for port and harbour development.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution deals with the impeachment procedure of the President?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Article 61**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 61** of the Indian Constitution provides the detailed procedure for the **impeachment of the President of India**.
 
• The President can be impeached for **violating the Constitution of India**.
 
• The process of impeachment involves a **two-thirds majority** in both Houses of Parliament.
 
• The procedure begins with a notice signed by a minimum of **one-fourth of the total number of members** of the House proposing the impeachment.
 
• The charges are investigated thoroughly and, upon confirmation, the President can be removed from office.
 
• This article ensures that the removal process is carried out in a **fair and systematic manner**.
 
• It is an important constitutional safeguard to maintain the integrity of the office of the President.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 66**__

 __
 
• **Article 66** deals with the **election of the Vice President of India**.
 
• The Vice President is elected by the members of **both Houses of Parliament** in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of a single transferable vote.
 
• The Vice President serves as the **Chairperson of the Rajya Sabha**.
 
 
 
• **Article 52**__
 __
 
• **Article 52** states that **India shall have a President**.
 
• The article establishes the office of the President as the head of the **Union Executive**.
 
• The President is the **highest constitutional authority** in India.
 
 
 
• **Article 54**__
 
 
• **Article 54** deals with the **election process of the President of India**.
 
• The President is elected by an electoral college consisting of the elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the States.
 
• The election is conducted in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of a **single transferable vote**.

questions.question: What has the Supreme Court of India ruled regarding the independence of tribunals?

options.text: Tribunals must be headed by sitting High Court judges to ensure credibility.
Tribunals are executive bodies and need not be independent of the executive.
Tribunals, being quasi-judicial bodies, must be independent of the executive, just like regular courts.
Tribunals can be managed by the subject-matter ministry to improve efficiency.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Tribunals, being quasi-judicial bodies, must be independent of the executive, just like regular courts**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Tribunals in India are established under various **statutory provisions** and play a critical role in adjudicating disputes related to specific areas such as **taxation, consumer protection, environment, and administrative law.**
 
• The Supreme Court of India has emphasized that tribunals, being **quasi-judicial bodies**, must maintain their **independence from the executive.** This ensures fairness, impartiality, and credibility in decision-making.
 
• The independence of tribunals is essential for safeguarding **constitutional rights** and maintaining the doctrine of separation of powers, as outlined in the **Constitution of India**.
 
• The judiciary has repeatedly stressed the need for structural and functional independence in tribunals to avoid undue influence or interference from the **executive branch of the government.**
 
• Tribunals are expected to have members with strong legal expertise, often including retired or serving judges, to ensure their decisions align with established legal principles and constitutional mandates.
 
• Key rulings by the Supreme Court, such as in the **R.K. Jain case** and **Madras Bar Association case**, have underlined the importance of ensuring that tribunals function autonomously without executive control.
 
• The independence of tribunals also helps in enhancing public trust and confidence in the justice delivery system, especially in specialized domains.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Option 1: Tribunals must be headed by sitting High Court judges to ensure credibility**__

 __
 
• This statement is **incorrect** as tribunals are not required to be headed by sitting High Court judges. However, retired judges or legal experts with vast experience often preside over tribunals to ensure their functioning is credible and adheres to legal norms.
 
• The Supreme Court has mandated the appointment of qualified members, but not necessarily sitting High Court judges, to ensure independence and expertise.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: Tribunals are executive bodies and need not be independent of the executive**__
 __
 
• This statement contradicts the principle of **judicial independence**. Tribunals, though established under executive provisions, must function independently to avoid bias and uphold the principles of **natural justice.**
 
• The Supreme Court has ruled that tribunals must be free from executive control to ensure fair adjudication of disputes.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: Tribunals can be managed by the subject-matter ministry to improve efficiency**__
 
 
• This option is incorrect as it undermines the independence of tribunals. Management by subject-matter ministries could lead to potential conflicts of interest and bias, which would compromise the tribunal’s impartiality.
 
• Tribunals must operate autonomously and cannot be directly managed by the executive branch or ministries.

questions.question: What was the effect of English education and western thought on Indian nationalism?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Ignited National Awakening**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **English education** and exposure to **Western thought** introduced Indians to concepts like **liberty, equality, fraternity, democracy, and human rights**.
 
• These values inspired many Indian leaders and reformers to question the prevailing social and political inequalities in the country.
 
• English education helped Indians gain access to **modern political ideologies** and understand the importance of self-rule and independence.
 
• The emergence of a class of educated Indians, referred to as the **Indian intelligentsia**, played a significant role in fostering the spirit of nationalism.
 
• It provided Indians with tools to challenge the **colonial exploitation** and assert their national identity.
 
• Western ideas, combined with the rich cultural heritage of India, led to the formation of organizations like the **Indian National Congress**, which became the vanguard of the Indian independence movement.
 
• Influential leaders such as **Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Dadabhai Naoroji, Gopal Krishna Gokhale, and Mahatma Gandhi** were deeply influenced by Western political theories and used them to shape India's nationalist agenda.
 
• English education also bridged regional divides, enabling Indians from various parts of the country to communicate and unite under a common cause.
 
• The **press and literature**, supported by English education, played a crucial role in spreading nationalist ideas and awakening the masses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Supported casteism**__

 __
 
• **Casteism** refers to discrimination based on caste. While English education exposed Indians to progressive ideas, it also led to debates about social reform.
 
• Some conservative elements used Western education to justify caste hierarchies, but overall, it contributed to diminishing casteism by promoting equality and unity.
 
 
 
• **Encouraged partition**__
 __
 
• Partition of India in **1947** was a result of complex political and communal factors, not directly related to English education or Western thought.
 
• However, English education did inadvertently highlight divisions, but it also helped foster unity among educated Indians.
 
 
 
• **Suppressed nationalism**__
 
 
• While British authorities tried to suppress nationalist movements using repressive measures, English education actually contributed to spreading nationalist ideas.
 
• Educated Indians used the knowledge gained from Western education to resist suppression and advocate for independence.

questions.question: Who presides over the sessions of the Vidhan Sabha in a State?

__
 
• The **Speaker** is the presiding officer of the **Vidhan Sabha**, also known as the Legislative Assembly, in Indian states.
 
• The Speaker is **elected by the members** of the Vidhan Sabha from among themselves, typically after the constitution of a new assembly following general elections.
 
• The Speaker is responsible for maintaining order and decorum during the proceedings of the assembly and ensures that the rules and guidelines are followed during debates and discussions.
 
• 
 
• The Speaker has the authority to make decisions on procedural matters and acts as the **neutral authority** to facilitate the smooth functioning of the legislative assembly.
 
• In the absence of the Speaker, the **Deputy Speaker** presides over the sessions.
 
• The Speaker plays a pivotal role in ensuring the democratic functioning of the legislature and safeguarding its independence.
 
• The Speaker does not vote in regular proceedings, except in case of a **tie**, where they cast the deciding vote.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

 __
 
• The **Governor** is the constitutional head of the state and acts as the representative of the President of India.
 
• The Governor’s primary role is to oversee the functioning of the state government and ensure compliance with the Constitution.
 
• The Governor does not preside over the Vidhan Sabha sessions but may address the assembly at the commencement of the first session of each year and after a general election.
 
 
 
• **The Chief Minister of the State**__
 __
 
• The **Chief Minister** is the elected head of the state government and leads the Council of Ministers.
 
• The Chief Minister is responsible for policy-making, administration, and governance but does not preside over the Vidhan Sabha sessions.
 
 
 
• **The Deputy Speaker by rotation**__
 
 
• The **Deputy Speaker** is elected by the members of the Vidhan Sabha and serves as the substitute presiding officer in the absence of the Speaker.
 
• However, the Deputy Speaker does not preside over sessions by rotation; they only perform the Speaker’s duties when required.
